subject: Archaeology
title: Cylinder Seals: Ancient Identity Badges
description: A micro-lesson that makes Cylinder Seals: Ancient Identity Badges usable.

hook.text: Mesopotamians rolled tiny carved cylinders across wet clay to sign documents — part stamp, part personal signature.

buildup.text: Each seal was unique. They showed gods, monsters, rituals, and daily life — carved in mirror image on stones as small as a thumb.

discovery.text: Over 100,000 cylinder seals survive in museums. They are one of the most common Mesopotamian artifacts found.

twist.text: Seals were so personal they were often buried with their owners. Losing your seal was like losing your identity.

climax.text: Seal impressions on tablets let archaeologists trace trade networks — the same seal appearing in different cities maps.

punchline.text: A carved stone the size of your thumb was your identity, your signature.

quiz.question: How do cylinder seal impressions help archaeologists?
options: They reveal the religious beliefs of each individual owner
The same seal in different cities maps a merchant's journey and trade networks
They contain hidden messages that explain Sumerian grammar
